findings.title: Backup-code login skips password verification and 2FA bypass is possible
findings.body: The password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is set (existing logic). The backup-code branch is reached with `credentials.backupCode` and no `totpCode`, so the password is verified there. However, a request carrying both a bogus `totpCode` and a `backupCode` skips the password check and then passes the backup-code branch, logging in with only a backup code and no password. The password-skip condition must also account for `backupCode`, or the backup-code branch must require the password.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is non-constant-time and codes are never invalidated reliably
findings.body: `indexOf` on the plaintext codes is a non-constant-time comparison. Used codes are set to `null` and re-encrypted via read-modify-write, so two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed. The rate limit is keyed per email only, so there is limited protection against guessing.

findings.title: Backup code input not validated or normalized
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a 500 if backupCode is not a string (e.g. a number or object). Used codes are stored as null, but the lookup does not guard against this. Add type validation. The same applies to credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.

findings.title: Backup codes regenerated on every setup call
findings.body: Setup writes fresh backup codes each time it runs, before 2FA is confirmed. The codes are returned to the client before the user has verified TOTP. If the user abandons setup, stale codes remain stored. Codes are shown only after enable succeeds, but they are held in client state and the old URL object is never revoked on close.

findings.title: Modal state not reset after enabling; codes persist
findings.body: After the user closes the backup-code step, backupCodes, backupCodesUrl and the form totpCode remain. The blob URL is never revoked on close. The form totpCode value is not cleared, so reopening can auto-submit the old 6-digit code via the watch effect. Dismissing the dialog via onOpenChange (outside click or Esc) bypasses resetState and onEnable, leaving the UI inconsistent with 2FA already enabled.

findings.title: BackupCode field is required, but TOTP is not, and the lost-access toggle button lacks type
findings.body: The toggle Button has no `type="button"`, so it may submit the form depending on the Button default. A submit would trigger validation and a disable request when the user only meant to switch modes.
